newsitem.title: USA: Powell leads Republicans as presidential choice.
newsitem.headline: Powell leads Republicans as presidential choice.

text.p: Retired Gen. Colin Powell was the top choice of Republican voters as their presidential candidate for the year 2000, according to a new poll released on Friday.

Powell led with 22 percent in the poll of 830 Republican voters conducted earlier this month by Fabrizio, McLaughlin and Associates, a Republican political consulting firm. The poll had a margin of error of plus or minus four percentage points.
Second in the poll with 14 percent was former housing secretary Jack Kemp, who was the running mate last year on the ticket of defeated Republican nominee Bob Dole.
Third was Dole's wife, Elizabeth, with 12 percent. Former Vice President Dan Quayle was next with 9 percent, ahead of Texas Gov. George Bush, son of the former president, who scored 7 percent.

Millionaire publisher Steve Forbes was next with 6 percent and conservative commentator Pat Buchanan registered 4 percent. Twelve percent were undecided and the rest of the votes were scattered among a number of other possible candidates.
